messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: page fired for service-api-prod - LB targets unhealthy (eu-west-1). Priority: P1. PagerDuty link: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD12345

carmen (oncall): acked. joining bridge in 2.

raj: I see spikes of TLS handshake failures from ALB logs starting 03:12 UTC. Health checks are failing with TLS errors, not 5xx from app. Example from /var/log/alb-health.log: 
```
2026-01-15T03:12:05Z ALB healthcheck: client=10.0.5.12 target=10.0.7.45 - TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure (err x509: certificate signed by unknown authority)
2026-01-15T03:12:06Z ALB healthcheck: client=10.0.5.12 target=10.0.7.46 - TLS handshake error: tls: certificate has expired
```

eli: I just ran a manual curl from inside the VPC against one backend ip and got TLS verify errors: 
```
curl -v https://10.0.7.45:8443/health --resolve service.prod.internal:8443:10.0.7.45
* About to connect() to 10.0.7.45 port 8443
* Connected to 10.0.7.45 (10.0.7.45) port 8443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: SSL: certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
* Closing connection 0
```

maya: Did we rotate certs last night for eu-west? I remember cadence job ran at 00:15UTC.

raj: Yes — we rotated the node certs and pushed new cert bundle to instances in eu-west. ALB is set to do healthchecks as HTTPS with SNI "service.prod.internal". Looks like the cert served from the backends doesn't include the right SAN for that SNI or chain is incomplete.

carmen (oncall): customers? impact?

support-bot: Monitoring alert: increase in 5xx rate for service-api-prod (eu-west-1) starting 03:11 UTC — approx 24 customers seeing failed requests, p95 latency spikes.

eli: Quick repro: openssl s_client -connect 10.0.7.45:8443 -servername service.prod.internal shows the server cert CN=internal.local and missing intermediate CA. Output snippet: 
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = internal.local
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=internal.local
   i:/CN=redwood-internal-ca
---
```

raj: Root cause hypothesis: automated cert rotation pushed an intermediate/cert chain mismatch to a subset of instances. ALB healthcheck verifies chain+SNI, so those targets flagged unhealthy. Because we have weighted routing across eu-west ALBs, traffic is being funneled to other targets and causing some 5xx from fallback.

carmen (oncall): mitigation options? can we change healthcheck to HTTP temporarily so ALB stops failing targets? or revert cert rotation? need low-risk immediate fix.

raj: We can do one of two low-risk moves: 
- Option A: Temporarily set ALB healthcheck to HTTP /health (port 8080) for eu-west target group (fast, no cert dependency) — immediate recovery of target state, but bypasses TLS verification for health checks (acceptable for short window).
- Option B: Re-deploy the previous cert bundle to the affected instances (safer long-term but rollback takes longer and may require instance restarts)

eli: I can flip the healthcheck to HTTP now. It's a config change on the ALB target group (no deploy). If we do that, we'll monitor for health states and customer error rate.

maya: +1 to HTTP switch. Do it and I'll watch metrics and error budget. Also start a rollback job simultaneously (raj + ops) so we have the certs fixed within 30m.

raj: Doing Option A now. Command I'm running (AWS CLI): 
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-eu/abcd --attributes Key=health.check.protocol,Value=HTTP Key=health.check.path,Value=/health
```

(5m later)

raj: Updated target group healthcheck to HTTP /health (port 8080) for tg-eu. Waiting for targets to re-evaluate.

incident-bot: Target group tg-eu: 3/6 healthy -> 6/6 healthy.

maya: p95 and error rates are starting to drop. support: can you confirm customer impact shrinking?

support-bot: Customer error notifications down from 24 to 3 impacted accounts over last 8 minutes. API 5xx rate back to baseline over last 6 minutes.

carmen (oncall): Good. raj, please schedule the cert rollback/repair on the affected instances and keep me posted. We need a timeline and owners. Also create an incident ticket (INC-2026-024) and postmortem owner.

raj: Creating rollback runbook and kicking off. Owner: raj (netops). ETA for full cert fix: 25-40 minutes. Actions: redeploy correct intermediate CA + restart service.

eli: Started a small smoke test across eu-west after health change and cert fix on one instance — ALB shows healthy and curl to service.prod.internal via ALB returns 200. 
```
curl -v https://service.prod.internal/health --resolve service.prod.internal:443:34.201.15.9
* Connected to service.prod.internal (34.201.15.9) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection established
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: service.prod.internal

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

carmen (oncall): OK marking P1 mitigated. We still have a root cause (cert rotation rigour) so we keep incident open until rollback done + postmortem assigned.

raj: Rollback complete on all affected hosts at 03:48 UTC. Verified chain + SANs. Reverting ALB healthcheck back to HTTPS with SNI. Command: 
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-eu/abcd --attributes Key=health.check.protocol,Value=HTTPS Key=health.check.path,Value=/health
```

incident-bot: Target group tg-eu: 6/6 healthy (HTTPS).

maya: Metrics stable for 15m, error budget unaffected now.

carmen (oncall): Good work. I'll create the incident ticket INC-2026-024 with timeline and owner raj for postmortem and follow-up: improve cert rotation validation step (include chain+SNI check in canary), add automated alert for partial cert chain mismatch.

support-bot: Notifying customers flagged earlier that service is restored.

carmen (oncall): closing on-call handoff in 10. Postmortem owner: raj. Please include rollout guardrails and a test that validates healthchecks using the exact SNI and chain the ALB will see.

raj: will do. closing the incident thread and will post the postmortem link here once ready.

eli: thanks everyone.

maya: :thumbsup:
